newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end thin session mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end thin session mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended a thinly traded session mixed after Standard & Poor's 500s staged a late rally in line with the U.S. Treasury bond market, traders and analysts said.

They traced the T-bond market's rally to comments by an unnamed Federal Reserve source that the Fed was close to adopting a core consumer price index (CPI) target as the basis for monetary policy. "The Fed views that a zero-to-two-percent range on core CPI is price stability," the source said.
Targeting core CPI as a guideline for policy has been "informally adopted within the Fed," the source told Reuters.
The comments briefly revived a trading session beset by thin volume due to the Yom Kippur holiday and nervousness ahead of the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

December S&Ps rose to 693.00 on short-covering after several large U.S. firms each bought about 500 to 700 contracts. One floor trader said December spiked up to 691.00 from 690.00 without one downtick.
Nikkei futures were slightly higher, but trade was light due to Japan's Autumn Equinox holiday, traders said.
They pegged fair value for the December futures contract at 6.05 points to cash, with arbitrage buy programs 0.80 above and arbitrage sell programs 0.80 below.

At the end of pit trade, December S&Ps were up 0.50 at 692.40, New Composites were up 0.40 at 368.00, Value Lines were down 0.70 at 638.20, Nikkeis were up 35 at 21,175.0 and Midcaps were up 0.05 at 240.65. Derivatives desk 312-408-8760;E-mail derivative@reuter.com
